children: New Delhi, Sept. 25 -- India is considering a plan to set up 15 additional overground liquefied natural gas (LNG) storage tanks across the country, boosting the nation's storage capacity by about two weeks , said three people aware of the plan.
The plan to build the critical storage capacity will require an investment of Rs.15,000 crore, adding to the country's existing capacity of 12 days across more than 20 tanks, the people said.
To support the project, the gas regulator may bring an additional surcharge of about 10% on the pipeline tariff paid by user sectors such as city gas and fertilizers, one of the people said.

The proposed storage comes as India relies on imports for nearly half of its natural gas consumption. LNG imports have become more expensive amid supply disruptions caused by the war in West Asia, pushing up the country's gas import bill even as import volumes have declined. Additional storage could also help protect consumers from a sharp increase in prices during a surge in global prices.

"Apart from ensuring availability, a key factor behind setting up reserves is to ensure affordable prices during a global price surge," said Manas Majumdar, leader, oil and gas sector, PwC India. If India imports LNG at a cheaper rate and stores, "it can be of great advantage when global prices are high. This will cushion the Indian market and consumers from higher global prices."

The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB), the petroleum and natural gas ministry and state-run gas marketing companies, including GAIL (India) Ltd, Indian Oil Corp. and Petronet LNG Ltd, are in talks to set up the storage capacity, the people said. The proposed reserves would add to the country's existing inventory of about 60 days of natural gas and LNG, including supplies in pipelines and in transit.

Currently, the there are two tariff rates in the country as per zones. The tariff rate for upto 300 kilometres is Rs.54 per million metric British thermal units (mmBtu) and Rs.110.86 beyond 300 kilometers.

"The tariffs for consumers may go up by Rs.4-5 per month. The cost of the surcharge will be democratized and will spread across the ecosystem. The eventual impact on the consumer would be not be significant," said the second person.

The person added that as the plan takes a concrete shape, it would be decided as to how the impact of the additional charge would be divided across the value chain to ensure minimum possible increase on the consumer tariff.

The development assumes significance as India has imposed restrictions on LNG use by industrial consumers amid supply disruptions, although these have since been gradually eased. Refiners and gas marketing companies could nevertheless face tighter supplies in the coming months as Europe's winter heating demand picks up, potentially adding to pressure on LNG prices.

Among key consumers, city gas distribution companies consume about 37 million standard cubic metres a day (mmscmd), including household PNG and CNG, while the fertilizer sector used 58 mmscmd and oil refiners consumed 22 mmscmd in FY25. CNG is largely catered to through domestic gas, while other sectors are highly dependent on imports.

Overall natural gas consumption in India is projected to reach 297-365 mmscmd by 2030 and 495-630 mmscmd by 2040. Industrial and commercial demand is expected to grow 10-15% by 2030, according to projections by the regulator.

"It is extremely important to create a storage and should be part of any emergency supply plan, particularly when you are heavily dependent on import of a particular commodity," said Anil Razdan, former additional secretary at the Union ministry of petroleum and natural gas. "Storage for LNG is something which was visualized two decades earlier but unfortunately, we did not act on it."
Mint earlier reported that the PNGRB proposed building overground natural gas storage facilities near existing LNG terminals to buffer against supply disruptions in West Asia caused by the war.
"The surcharge would support the capex of the marketing companies," the second person said, adding that the storage facilities would be set up near LNG regasification terminals in the country.

India currently has eight operational onshore LNG terminals, with combined regasification capacity of 52.7 million metric tonnes per annum (mmtpa), equivalent to about 190 mmscmd. Several other land-based terminals and floating storage regasification units (FSRUs) are at various stages of development.

Around 55% of India's LPG imports were sourced from West Asia and routed through the Strait of Hormuz before the war.Natural gas imports stood at $13.4 billion in FY26, according to commerce ministry data, of which Qatar accounted for about 42%.

In FY27, Qatar accounts for about 3.8% of LNG imports. Currently, natural gas comprises of 6% India's energy basket, and the government aims to raise its share to 15% by 2030.Currently, the US is the top supplier of LNG to India, resulting in a higher import bill because of longer voyage times and higher freight charges.
Queries emailed to spokespersons for the Union ministry of petroleum and natural gas, PNGRB, Indian Oil Corp., GAIL (India) Ltd, Petronet LNG remained unanswered at press time.
Razdan said the cost of developing the infrastructure would eventually be transferred to the consumer, but that a moderate increase should not materially affect them.

"The cost of it has to be imposed on the consumer, and as long as it is moderate and affordable I would say given the situation it is not unreasonable. We already have a pipeline network and this kind of a fallback is absolutely necessary," he said.

Natural gas imports stood at $13.3 billion in FY26, according to data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), of which Qatar accounted for about 42%. In FY27, Qatar accounts for about 3.8% of LNG imports. Currently, natural gas comprises of 6% India's energy basket, and the government aims to raise its share to 15% by 2030.
Rajesh Mediratta, managing director and chief executive officer of Indian Gas Exchange, said growing demand for natural gas would require additional storage capacity.
"Demand is growing in CNG and PNG, along with fertilizer, industrial and commercial demand too. Additional reserves would be helpful for the country," he said.

title: India plans LNG storage boost, a pipeline tariff surcharge to support
